q_en: How do I find a word I do not know in a dictionary?
q_ar: كَيْفَ أَجِدُ كَلِمَةً لَا أَعْرِفُهَا فِي الْمُعْجَمِ؟
not_yet: Dictionaries in another order (by the last letter, or by meaning).
Roots with a weak letter or a hamza: look under the other letters too.
The long entries of a big dictionary: they say more than you can use yet.
not_yet_ar: مَعَاجِمُ بِتَرْتِيبٍ آخَرَ: بِآخِرِ الْجَذْرِ أَوْ بِالْمَعْنَى.
جُذُورٌ فِيهَا حَرْفُ عِلَّةٍ أَوْ هَمْزَةٌ: اِبْحَثْ تَحْتَ الْحُرُوفِ الْأُخْرَى أَيْضًا.
الْمَوَادُّ الطَّوِيلَةُ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ الْكَبِيرِ: فِيهَا أَكْثَرُ مِمَّا تَسْتَعْمِلُ الْآنَ.

slides.head_en: Look: four long words. What is the word inside?
slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: أَرْبَعُ كَلِمَاتٍ طَوِيلَةٍ. مَا الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي فِيهَا؟
sents: And those who ask forgiveness remember Allah.
The father opened the library for the travellers.
Their learning is better than their play.
The youngest of them listens to the Habib.

lines: Which letters of وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرُونَ are not the word itself?
أَيُّ حُرُوفِ «وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرُونَ» لَيْسَتْ مِنْ أَصْلِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
How many letters stay when you take them away?
Does a dictionary order words by their first letter, or by the root?
هَلْ يُرَتِّبُ الْمُعْجَمُ الْكَلِمَاتِ بِأَوَّلِ حَرْفٍ أَمْ بِالْجَذْرِ؟

cards.def_ar: اِنْزَعِ الْحُرُوفَ الصَّغِيرَةَ فِي الْأَوَّلِ وَالنِّهَايَةَ فِي الْآخِرِ.
cards.def_en: take off the little words in front (and, the, with, for) and the endings behind (his, their, plural)

cards.def_ar: اِنْزَعْ حُرُوفَ الشَّكْلِ أَيْضًا: يَبْقَى ثَلَاثَةُ حُرُوفٍ.
cards.def_en: take off the extra letters of the shape too: three letters stay

cards.def_ar: اِفْتَحِ الْمُعْجَمَ: الْحَرْفُ الْأَوَّلُ، ثُمَّ الثَّانِي، ثُمَّ الثَّالِثُ.
cards.def_en: open the dictionary at the first root letter, then the second, then the third. Find the word by its shape.

slides.head_en: From the long word to the root
slides.note: A plural that breaks (مَسَاجِد) goes back to its singular before you look for the root.
slides.note_ar: الْجَمْعُ الْمُكَسَّرُ (مَسَاجِد) نَرُدُّهُ إِلَى مُفْرَدِهِ (مَسْجِد) قَبْلَ أَنْ نَبْحَثَ عَنِ الْجَذْرِ.

slides.head_en: One root, one place in the dictionary
slides.head_ar: جَذْرٌ وَاحِدٌ، مَكَانٌ وَاحِدٌ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ
slides.note: A dictionary keeps all of these together under ع ل م, one after another by shape.
slides.note_ar: يَجْمَعُ الْمُعْجَمُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ كُلَّهَا تَحْتَ ع ل م، وَاحِدَةً بَعْدَ أُخْرَى حَسَبَ الشَّكْلِ.

slides.head_en: Level 6 on one page: what each shape adds
slides.head_ar: الْمُسْتَوَى السَّادِسُ فِي صَفْحَةٍ: مَاذَا يَزِيدُ كُلُّ شَكْلٍ؟
rows: done to him; the doer is not named
it happens · for himself · asks for
slides.note: Whatever the shape, the root is still three letters. Take the shape off, and the dictionary opens.
slides.note_ar: مَهْمَا كَانَ الشَّكْلُ فَالْجَذْرُ ثَلَاثَةُ حُرُوفٍ. اِنْزَعِ الشَّكْلَ فَيُفْتَحُ لَكَ الْمُعْجَمُ.

slides.why: A student looks for this word under م, its first letter, and finds nothing. Wrong! Take off الْ, the shape letters and the plural ending: the root is غ ف ر. Look under غ.
slides.why_ar: بَحَثَ طَالِبٌ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ تَحْتَ الْمِيمِ وَلَمْ يَجِدْهَا. خَطَأٌ! اِنْزَعِ «الْ» وَحُرُوفَ الشَّكْلِ وَنِهَايَةَ الْجَمْعِ: الْجَذْرُ غ ف ر. اُنْظُرْ تَحْتَ الْغَيْنِ.

lines: to study: he read and understood.
ذَكَرَ، يَذْكُرُ، ذِكْرًا: حَفِظَ شَيْئًا فِي قَلْبِهِ أَوْ قَالَهُ.
to remember, to mention: he kept something in his heart or said it.
غَفَرَ، يَغْفِرُ، غَفْرًا وَمَغْفِرَةً: سَتَرَ وَعَفَا.
to forgive: he covered over and pardoned.
كَتَبَ، يَكْتُبُ، كِتَابَةً: رَسَمَ الْكَلِمَاتِ بِالْقَلَمِ.
to write: he drew the words with the pen.

slides.big_en: Strip it. Find the root. Look it up.
slides.big_ar: اِنْزَعْ. اِعْرِفِ الْجَذْرَ. اُنْظُرْ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ.
slides.small: Now the checkpoint: a story, two dictionary pages, and unseen lines of every kind you have met in Level 6.
slides.small_ar: الْآنَ الِاخْتِبَارُ: قِصَّةٌ وَصَفْحَتَانِ مِنْ مُعْجَمٍ وَأَسْطُرٌ جَدِيدَةٌ مِنْ كُلِّ نَوْعٍ قَرَأْتَهُ فِي الْمُسْتَوَى السَّادِسِ.

can: I can take a long word apart (little words, endings, shape) and find its three root letters.
I can find a word in a dictionary that is kept in root order, and read its entry.
I can read the shape of a verb or noun and say what it adds (passive, Forms II–X, place, tool, little, belonging, more).
I can read a short unseen line (a saying, a ḥadīth, a prayer, the start of a book) with a short gloss and say what it means.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُفَكِّكَ كَلِمَةً طَوِيلَةً (حُرُوفٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَنِهَايَاتٌ وَشَكْلٌ) وَأَجِدَ حُرُوفَ جَذْرِهَا الثَّلَاثَةَ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ كَلِمَةً فِي مُعْجَمٍ مُرَتَّبٍ بِالْجُذُورِ وَأَقْرَأَ مَادَّتَهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ شَكْلَ الْفِعْلِ أَوِ الِاسْمِ وَأَقُولَ مَاذَا يَزِيدُ (الْمَجْهُولُ وَالْأَفْعَالُ الْمَزِيدَةُ وَالْمَكَانُ وَالْأَدَاةُ وَالتَّصْغِيرُ وَالنِّسْبَةُ وَالتَّفْضِيلُ).
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ سَطْرًا جَدِيدًا قَصِيرًا (حِكْمَةً أَوْ حَدِيثًا أَوْ دُعَاءً أَوْ بِدَايَةَ كِتَابٍ) مَعَ شَرْحٍ قَصِيرٍ وَأَقُولَ مَعْنَاهُ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: A short text: a word Ahmad did not know. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَقَرَأَ كِتَابًا قَدِيمًا.
In the evening Ahmad sat in the library and read an old book.
He found in it a new word: al-mustamiʿūn.
لَمْ يَسْأَلْ أَبَاهُ، بَلْ فَتَحَ الْمُعْجَمَ.
He did not ask his father; rather, he opened the dictionary.
قَالَ لِنَفْسِهِ: هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ جَذْرِ سَمِعَ، فَأَنْظُرُ فِي بَابِ السِّينِ.
He said to himself: This word is from the root of سَمِعَ (“he heard”), so I will look in the chapter of the letter sīn.
وَوَجَدَ الْمَعْنَى: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
And he found the meaning: the listeners are those who hear the Habib in the majlis.
And he wrote the meaning of the word in his book.
ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ: فَهِمْتُ الْكَلِمَةَ وَحْدِي.
Then he went back to his father and said: I understood the word by myself.
قَالَ أَبُوهُ: أَنْتَ الْآنَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
His father said: You are now a seeker of knowledge.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.en: Where did Ahmad sit, and what did he read?
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَاذَا قَرَأَ؟
options: In the library; an old book.
items.answer: In the library; an old book.
items.model: In the library; an old book.

items.en: What new word did he find?
items.ar_q: أَيَّةَ كَلِمَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ وَجَدَ؟
options: From سَمِعَ, under sīn (س), the first letter of the root.

items.en: Did he ask his father? What did he do instead?
items.ar_q: هَلْ سَأَلَ أَبَاهُ؟ مَاذَا فَعَلَ؟
options: In the library; an old book.

items.en: Which verb is the word from? Under which letter did he look?
items.ar_q: الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ؟ تَحْتَ أَيِّ حَرْفٍ نَظَرَ؟
options: From سَمِعَ, under sīn (س), the first letter of the root.
In the library; an old book.
items.answer: From سَمِعَ, under sīn (س), the first letter of the root.
items.model: From سَمِعَ, under sīn (س), the first letter of the root.

items.en: True or false?
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
items.model: False. He looked in the chapter of sīn (not ʿayn).
items.note: He looked in the chapter of sīn (not ʿayn).

items.en: What did he write in his book?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا كَتَبَ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟
options: In the library; an old book.

items.en: Root hunt: find the words in lines 4 and 5 that share the root س م ع with الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ.
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٤ وَ٥ لَهُمَا الْجَذْرُ نَفْسُهُ فِي «الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ»: س م ع.
options: In the library; an old book.

items.en: ★ Why did Ahmad not look under م, the first letter of الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا لَمْ يَنْظُرْ أَحْمَدُ تَحْتَ الْمِيمِ؟
items.model: Because the م belongs to the shape (the doer prefix), not to the root. A dictionary is in root order: س م ع.

items.en: ★ What does his father mean by “You are now a seeker of knowledge”?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يَقْصِدُ أَبُوهُ بِقَوْلِهِ «أَنْتَ الْآنَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ»؟
items.model: He sees that Ahmad found the meaning by himself, the way a student of knowledge works.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A page of a dictionary. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: to serve: he worked for people.
to ask: he asked for an answer.
سَكَنَ، يَسْكُنُ: جَلَسَ فِي بَيْتٍ وَقْتًا طَوِيلًا.
to live (in a place): he sat in a house for a long time.
the dwelling: a house where people live.
to do, to work: he did something.
the key: a thing we open the door with.
sections.cite: Course text: entries written for the course in the style of a school dictionary, in root order; no printed source.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟
items.model: A page of a dictionary: entries in root order, with the past, the present and the meaning.

items.en: Translate the first entry.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ الْمَادَّةَ الْأُولَى.
options: to serve: he worked for people.
Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.
A thing we open the door with.
items.answer: to serve: he worked for people.
items.model: to serve: he worked for people.

items.en: Under which entry would you find سُؤَال (“a question”)? Which root?
items.ar_q: تَحْتَ أَيِّ مَادَّةٍ تَجِدُ «سُؤَالًا»؟ مَا جَذْرُهَا؟
options: to serve: he worked for people.
Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.
A thing we open the door with.
items.answer: Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.
items.model: Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.

items.en: What is a مِفْتَاح, according to the page?
items.ar_q: مَا الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي هَذِهِ الصَّفْحَةِ؟
options: to serve: he worked for people.
Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.
A thing we open the door with.
items.answer: A thing we open the door with.
items.model: A thing we open the door with.

items.en: Which two verbs are entered under the letter س? Which one comes first, and why?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ فِعْلَيْنِ تَحْتَ السِّينِ؟ أَيُّهُمَا أَوَّلًا؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
items.model: سَأَلَ (س أ ل) comes before سَكَنَ (س ك ن): the second letter decides: أ comes before ك.

items.en: True or false?
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟

items.en: Root hunt: which word on the page shares its root with the verb سَكَنَ?
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الصَّفْحَةِ جَذْرُهَا مِثْلُ سَكَنَ.
options: Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.
to serve: he worked for people.
A thing we open the door with.

items.en: ★ The entry الْمَسْكَنُ stands right under the verb سَكَنَ. Why is a noun listed under a verb?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَأْتِي الِاسْمُ «الْمَسْكَنُ» تَحْتَ الْفِعْلِ «سَكَنَ»؟
items.model: Both come from the root س ك ن; the dictionary keeps a whole root family together.

items.en: ★ Each verb entry gives the present as well as the past. What does the present show that the past does not?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ الْمُعْجَمُ الْمُضَارِعَ مَعَ الْمَاضِي؟
items.model: The vowel on the middle root letter in the present (ـَ in يَسْأَلُ and يَعْمَلُ, ـُ in يَخْدُمُ): the past does not tell you which it is.

sections.name: C
sections.en: Unseen lines (1): three sayings. Read them aloud, then answer.
lines: مَنْ حَفِظَ الْفُؤَادَ حُفِظَ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ.
Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.
Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
الْعِلْمُ عَلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَعْمَلَ بِهِ، فَإِذَا عَمِلْتَ بِهِ كَانَ الْعِلْمُ لَكَ.
Knowledge is against you until you act on it; when you act on it, it is for you.
sections.source: al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya (Kitāb al-Ḥikam of Imam al-Ḥaddād)
sections.cite: al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (1044–1132 H), Kitāb al-Ḥikam (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, 8), Dār al-Ḥāwī, 1st ed. 1413 H, 2nd ed. 1418 H (title page of the Shamela copy; SSD Master Library [184340]), p. 1/31; al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, p. 1/22; al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, p. 1/30. Consonants checked against the copy; vowelled for learners.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
options: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.
Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
items.answer: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.
items.model: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.

items.en: Translate line 2.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
options: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.
items.answer: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
items.model: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: Wise sayings (ḥikam) of Imam al-Ḥaddād, from his book al-Ḥikam.

items.en: In line 3, what is “against you” until you act on it?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ: مَاذَا يَكُونُ «عَلَيْكَ» حَتَّى تَعْمَلَ بِهِ؟
options: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.

items.en: In line 1, how is حُفِظَ different from حَفِظَ?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: مَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ حُفِظَ وَحَفِظَ؟
items.model: It is the passive (Lesson 42): “is guarded”; the guard is not named. حَفِظَ = he guarded, he memorised.

items.en: Root hunt: line 3 has two verbs built on the root ع م ل. Find them.
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ عَنْ فِعْلَيْنِ جَذْرُهُمَا ع م ل.
options: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.
Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.

items.en: ★ أَصْلَحَ is on the shape of Form IV. What idea in the root ص ل ح (as in صَالِح) does it make into an action?
items.ar_q: ★ أَصْلَحَ عَلَى شَكْلِ أَفْعَلَ. مَا فِكْرَةُ الْجَذْرِ ص ل ح (كَمَا فِي صَالِح)؟
items.model: Goodness, rightness: أَصْلَحَ = he made it right, he mended it.

items.en: ★ Line 3 sets “against you” against “for you”. What turns the knowledge from one into the other?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُحَوِّلُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْ «عَلَيْكَ» إِلَى «لَكَ»؟
items.model: Acting on it (عَمِلْتَ بِهِ). Knowledge that is not acted on is a proof against its owner; acted on, it is for him.

sections.name: D
sections.en: Unseen lines (2): a ḥadīth clause and two lines of prayer. Read them aloud, then answer.
lines: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden.
يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ
O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, make us die in the religion of Islam.
Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds ...
sections.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Rātib of Imam al-Ḥaddād; al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa
sections.cite: Line 1: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2699: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786; the card gives no year), 8/71 (Dār al-Jīl no. 7028); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 2699, 4/2074 (a clause of the ḥadīth «مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً ...»; the same clause opens the Risāla al-Jāmiʿa after «طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ»)  Line 2: Rātib al-Ḥaddād, 15th dhikr (said seven times): Rātib al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, called Sabīl al-Saʿāda wa-l-Falāḥ fī Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa-l-Ṣabāḥ, in the Shamela copy 'Awrād wa-Aḥzāb' (SSD Master Library [184180], from the loose .bok file; printed edition not identified), part 2, p. 2/3; Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād p. 137 (heading seen on the page image)  Line 3: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa, Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī al-ʿAlawī (1069–1145 H), al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr wa-l-Tawzīʿ, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (title page of the Shamela copy; no year given; SSD Master Library [182670]), p. 1/2 (the opening doxology) Course cut: line 3 is cut after رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ and marked with “...”.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
items.model: Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden.

items.en: Translate line 2.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, make us die in the religion of Islam.

items.en: The three lines are of three kinds: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ, a prayer, and the opening of a book. Which is which?
items.ar_q: الْأَسْطُرُ الثَّلَاثَةُ ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ: حَدِيثٌ وَدُعَاءٌ وَبِدَايَةُ كِتَابٍ. أَيُّ سَطْرٍ مِنْ أَيِّ نَوْعٍ؟
items.model: Line 1: the Prophet’s ﷺ saying (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim). Line 2: a prayer (from the Rātib). Line 3: the opening praise of a book (al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa).

items.en: In line 1, what does Allah make easy, and for whom?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: مَاذَا يُسَهِّلُ اللَّهُ؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
items.model: A path to the Garden, for whoever follows a path seeking knowledge.

items.en: Root hunt: يَلْتَمِسُ is on the shape of Form VIII (like اِجْتَمَعَ). What is its root?
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ عَنْ جَذْرِ يَلْتَمِسُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى شَكْلِ اِجْتَمَعَ.
items.model: ل م س (the verb is اِلْتَمَسَ: he sought).

items.en: In line 3, what is the praise addressed to?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ: لِمَنِ الْحَمْدُ؟
items.model: To Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

items.en: ★ The word طَرِيقًا is in line 1 twice. How does the second “path” differ from the first?
items.ar_q: ★ جَاءَتْ كَلِمَةُ «طَرِيقًا» مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. بِمَ يَخْتَلِفُ الثَّانِي عَنِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
items.model: The first is the way the man walks (his seeking); the second is the path Allah makes easy for him, to the Garden.

items.en: ★ Where else have you read the words الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ? What does that tell you about the opening of a book?
items.ar_q: ★ أَيْنَ قَرَأْتَ «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ» مِنْ قَبْلُ؟ وَمَاذَا يُخْبِرُكَ ذَلِكَ عَنْ بِدَايَةِ الْكِتَابِ؟
items.model: In sūrat al-Fātiḥa. A book often opens with praise, as the Qur’an does.

lines: حَفِظَ، يَحْفَظُ، حِفْظًا: جَعَلَ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
to memorise: he put the words in his heart.
رَجَعَ، يَرْجِعُ: ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي جَاءَ مِنْهُ.
to return: he went to the place he came from.
زَارَ، يَزُورُ، زِيَارَةً: ذَهَبَ إِلَى صَدِيقٍ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ.
to visit: he went to a friend and sat with him.
to worship: he prayed and prostrated to Allah.
to look: he saw with his eye.

sections.name: AA
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–98
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.

items.en: Translate the two new lines into English.
items.model: The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word. Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.

items.en: To find a word in the dictionary, what must you find first?
items.model: Its root: strip the extra letters and the pattern, then look up the root.

items.en: In the first new line, which verb means “he found”? Give its root.
Write in Arabic: The boy found the meaning of the word.
